Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 
23 January, 2024 
 In The Court Of Mr. Sanjay Gargi
 Principal District & Sessions Judge,
 New Delhi District,
 Patiala House Courts, New Delhi
Fsat04/2021
Cnr No. Dlnd010042432021
1. Sh. Rajesh Gupta
S/o. Sh. Birbal Dass
2. Sh. Akash Gupta
S/o. Late Sh. Prem Lal Gupta,
Both At : M/s. Bikaner Sweet House,
Shop No. F.14/17, Model TownII,
Delhi110009 ........ Appellants
 Versus
State
Through Food Safety Officer,
Department of Food Safety,
Govt. of Nct of Delhi, 8th Floor,
Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Palace,
New Delhi110001. ....... Respondent
 Date of Institution : 25.06.2021 
 Date of hearing arguments : 16.01.2024  Date of Judgment : 23.01.2024 Appearances:
Sh. Sukrit Gupta, Ld. Counsel for the appellants. 
Sh. P.N. Pandey, Ld. SPP for the State/Respondent along with Sh. S.P. Singh, DO.
JUDGMENT 1. This order shall decide the present appeal preferred by the appellants under Section 71 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (as amended upto date) hereinafter referred as 'FSS Act')
assailing the impugned order No. ADM/N/FSS/05/2020/44334435 dated 07.04.2021 passed by Sh. Nitin Jindal, Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate (District North), Delhi, whereby penalty of Rs.1,50,000/ (Rupees One Lac Fifty Thousand only) has been imposed upon the appellants in terms of Rule 3.1.2(1) of Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011 with directions that said penalty should be deposited within 07 days from the date of receipt of this order failing which recovery proceedings will be initiated against them. BRIEF FACTS Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/
1 2. It is stated that on 26.04.2019, a sample of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" was taken by Sh. S.P.
Singh along with Sh. Hukum Singh, the then Food Safety Officers for its analysis from appellant No.2 i.e. Sh. Akash Gupta S/o. Late Sh. Prem Lal Gupta, FBOcumManager of M/s. Bikaner Sweet House, Shop No. F.14/17, Model TownII, Delhi110009. It is alleged that the said food article was stored for sale when its sample was taken from the said shop and it consisted of four sealed packs of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" each of 400 grams bearing identical label declaration. It is further alleged that Sh. S.P. Singh, the then FSO made endeavour to join the public witnesses by requesting them but when none came forward, Sh. Hukum Singh the then Food Officer joined as a witness in sample proceedings. It is alleged that panchnama and notice in FormVA was prepared at the spot and copy of the notice was given to appellant No.2 along with price of Rs.592/ and all the documents prepared in this regard were read over and explained to appellant No.2 in Hindi who signed the same after understanding it. Thereafter, one part of the sample bearing No.232/1036/18/2019 and DO Code No.02/DO20/13434 in intact condition along with copy of memo in FormVI were sent to Food Analyst, Delhi for analysis on 29.04.2019 and vide its report bearing No.FSS/634/2019 dated 07.05.2019, the Food Analyst reported that the sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.7, 2.2.2.2, 2.2.2.3, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.8 and 2.2.2.10 of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011. The Food Analyst also reported that the sample was without declaration of FSSAI Logo and License No., List of Ingredients, Nutritional Information, Vegetarian Symbol, Batch No. and Best Before. A copy of this report was sent to the FBO with an opportunity to file appeal against the said report but none of the appellants preferred any appeal against it. On 02.02.2021, the appellants filed reply to the application and had contended as follows :
i) That during the sample proceedings, the FSO has not tried to associate any public witnesses;
ii) That the sample of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" was in a loose condition &
iii) That it has been also objected that all the documents prepared at the spot were read over and explained to FBO in Hindi and the respondent was not present at the spot at the time of proceedings. 
GROUNDS OF APPEAL 3. The appellants have assailed the impugned order passed by the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. 
District Magistrate on the ground that it is not only in ignorance of the pleadings placed before him but also in contravention to the settled law and is based on surmises and conjectures without appreciating the evidence and pleading of the parties . It is alleged that Adjudicating Officer/Addl.
District Magistrate has failed to appreciate that though, as per the respondent, the pack of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" was originally sealed however no picture/video of the same has been placed on record showing that it was originally sealed. The Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate has also failed to appreciate that the appellants have explicitly stated that sample of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)"
Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/
2 were kept loose and not in prepackaged condition and were packed as per the desired quantity to be purchased by the customer and thus the sample cannot be treated as sample originally sealed or prepared at the instance of the manufacturer and hence does not fall under the ambit of Section 23, Section 26(1), Section 26(2)
and Section 27 read with Section 3(1)(zf)(B)
(ii) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006. It is further alleged that as per Rule 3.1.2.(3) of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2011, "every order made under Rule 3.1.2.(1) shall specify the provisions of the act or the rules or the regulations in respect of which the offence has taken place and shall contain brief reasons for such decisions". However, the impugned order does not find any mention of the submissions advanced by the appellants and contentions made in the pleadings. The Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate further failed to appreciate that as per the report dated 07.05.2019 of the Food Analyst, no deficiencies were found in the food sample and same was passed in all tests and found to be fit and safe for human consumption. It is further alleged that the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate has failed to appreciate that no public witness was engaged by the respondent to prove their testimony and instead made a witness amongst themselves. 
It is mentioned that vide Notification No. F.No.13(29)2019/Milk/RCD/FSSAI dated 25.09.2020 of FSSAI, the appellants have now started displaying the manufacturing and best before date and other relevant information on it. 
ARGUMENTS 4. Heard the arguments of Sh. Sukrit Gupta, Ld. Counsel for the appellant, Sh. P.N. Pandey, Ld. SPP for the State/Respondent along with Sh. S.P. Singh, DO for the State/respondent. I have gone through the record of the Adjudicating Officer, record of the present appeal and documents filed therewith. 
DECISION 5. The opinion vide report No.FSS/634/2019 dated 07.05.2019 of the Food Analyst, Department of Food Safety, Government of NCT of Delhi, is as follows :
"Label : Without declaration of FSSAI Logo & License No., List of Ingredients,
Nutritional Information, Vegetarian Symbol, Batch No. and Best Before".
"The sample is misbranded because there is violation of Regulation No.2.2.1.7,
2.2.2.2, 2.2.2.3, 2.2.2.4, 2.2.2.8 and 2.2.2.10 of The Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulation, 2011.
6. On the basis of the report of the Food Analyst, the Adjudicating Officer/Addl.
District Magistrate (District North), Delhi, has come to the conclusion that Food Business Operators i.e. appellants herein had committed offence of selling Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/
3 misbranded food articles in violation of Section 23, Section 26(1), Section 26(2) and Section 27 read with Section 3(1) (zf) (B)(ii) of the Food Safety and Standards Act,
2006, punishable under Section 52 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 and thus imposed penalty of Rs.1,50,000/ (Rupees One lac Fifty Thousand only) in terms of Rule 3.1.2(1) of Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
7. One of the main contention raised on behalf of the appellant is that the "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" were kept loose and not in packaged condition as alleged by the respondent. 
It is stated that the sample was put in the transparent box by the officials of the respondent whereas the appellants were selling the product as per the desired quantity to be purchased by the customers. 
To better appreciate the facts, the sample sealed by the officials of respondent were called in the court and after breaking the seal, a round transparent pack was taken out. The observation made vide order dated 16.01.2024 by this court is reproduced as follows :
"A round transparent pack duly sealed with the transparent tape is taken out. On the top of it, it bears sticker of:-
BIKANER Sweet House F-14/17 Model Town-II.
On the bottom of it, it bears following two stickers:-
This Pack is Exclusively Prepared at Bikaner Sweet House Model Town BIKANER SWEET HOUSE F-14/17, Model Town lind, New Delhi-110009 Ph:011-27110558,
27245374 Customer Care no. :9868168476 Email:rajesh.gupta1312@yahoo.com KAJU PISTA DANDA QUANTITY-400gm RATE-148/0 MFD. DATE Apr 2019 Thereafter a round pack is returned to the Ld. SPP for the respondent to be sealed with the court seal". 
8. The observation made by this court in its order dated 16.01.2024 mentioned above, belies the submission made by Ld. Counsel for the appellants. The fixation of the sticker at the bottom of the pack clearly mentions that this is a pack of "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" containing 400 grams quantity and also rate is found mentioned. 
9. The other contention raised on behalf of the appellants is that the Adjudicating Officer, as per law,
is required to give the reasons for his decision but absolutely no reason has been given by him in the impugned order. As pointed out by Ld. Counsel for the appellants, Rule 3.1.2.(3) of Food Safety and Standards Act provides that every order made under this rule shall specify the provisions of this Act and the rules and regulations in respect of which the offence has taken place and shall contain brief reasons for such decision. Perusal of the impugned order reveals that submissions made by appellants in its counter reply/written submissions are not at all discussed by the Adjudicating Officer in this impugned order. As already mentioned that Rule 3.1.2.(3) of the Act desires that the Adjudicating Authority is required to give brief reasons for its decision. Moreover, principles of Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/
4 natural justice provide that no one should be condemn unheard. Hearing given to the affected party means that not only factum of giving hearing to him should be mentioned but his representations,
written or oral, are also required to be considered and reasons for not accepting the submissions are required to be mentioned. It is observed that in most of the cases, the Adjudicating Officers are not giving reasons for disbelieving the submissions made by the affected private party. 
10. Though the Adjudicating Officer has not given the reasons on which he has based his impugned order but despite that I find no illegality in the impugned order solely on this count. 
11. Other contention raised on behalf of the appellants is that no public witness was engaged by the respondent to prove their case and instead of that, they have made their own Officer a witness to the proceedings. The joining of a public witness is not a prerequisite as per law while sealing the product seized from the FBO. I find no reason to assume that the respondent had put the "Kaju Pista Danda (Biscuits)" in the sealed plastic pack with the sole purpose to falsely implicate the appellants in this case. 
12. In view of the aforesaid reasons, I find no merit in this appeal and same is thereby dismissed. 
13. The record of the Adjudicating Officer/Addl. District Magistrate along-with copy of this Judgment be sent back. File of appeal be consigned to Record Room.

on the ground that it is not only in ignorance of the pleadings placed before him but also in contravention to the settled law and is based on surmises and conjectures without appreciating the evidence and pleading of the parties
. It is alleged that Adjudicating Officer/Addl.

summary.ANALYSIS:
As already mentioned that Rule 3.1.2.(3) of the Act desires that the Adjudicating Authority is required to give brief reasons for its decision.
Moreover, principles of Rajesh Gupta And Anr vs State, Through Food Safety Officer on 23 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50018580/
4 natural justice provide that no one should be condemn unheard.
The joining of a public witness is not a prerequisite as per law while sealing the product seized from the FBO.
